snippets.text: Arena says Meta's Muse Spark Open (Max) is the top US open model in its Code Arena WebDev ranking, with 1511 points, priced at $1.25 and $4.25 per million input and output tokens.
snippets.why: It is the first open-weight Muse Spark model, and Arena says it scores 156 points above Meta's earlier open model, Muse Glimmer.

snippets.text: Tibo Sottiaux (@thsottiaux) says Codex and Work now give users more effective usage, citing context reuse across subagents, longer caching and better request routing that raise cache hits.
snippets.why: The post, labelled Day 12 of a series, had 1,112 likes within hours, and it also says GPT-6 Pro was improved for all Pro users.

snippets.text: Politico reports Anthropic has written its own bill to regulate frontier AI and is pitching it to members of Congress, according to a post by Andrew Curran that cites the report.
snippets.why: Politico's own article was not reachable for this item, so the bill's contents are unconfirmed here.

snippets.text: SemiAnalysis says ByteDance gave apps 30 days to opt out of its Doubao phone agent and 155 did, including WeChat, Taobao, Alipay, DeepSeek and Kimi.
snippets.why: The same post says Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent, so it frames access for AI agents as a growing fight between apps and assistants.

snippets.text: Nvidia says its first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm is out, and claims RTX Spark runs coding agents 4.6x faster than Intel's Panther Lake 12Xe.
snippets.why: The figures come from Nvidia's own developer blog and use its AA-AgentPerf-local test with Qwen3.8-27B, so they await independent checks.

snippets.text: Tongyi-MAI released OpenGCUA, an Apache-2.0 research preview with code and trajectories from eight frontier models, and says its approach lifts mean OSWorld-v2 partial score from 45.3 to 64.9.
snippets.why: The repo ships no model yet, only agents, a macOS harness and data, and the gains are the authors' own evaluation.

snippets.text: International Cyber Digest says Unit 42 found hackers spied on government Linux servers for months using AI-written code, and left the AI's chats behind; a fake sudo prompt saved admin passwords.
snippets.why: The claim comes from a social post summarising the report, which was not located, so details are unverified.
